landmarks.description: Earth's highest mountain
landmarks.summary: Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level. It lies in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas and marks part of the China–Nepal border at its summit. 86 m.

landmarks.name: Taj Mahal
landmarks.description: Marble mausoleum in Agra, India
landmarks.summary: The Taj Mahal is an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the right bank of the river Yamuna in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India. It was commissioned in 1631 by the fifth Mughal emperor, Shah Jahan, to house the tomb of his late wife, Mumtaz Mahal; it also houses the tomb of Shah Jahan himself.

landmarks.name: Eiffel Tower
landmarks.description: Tower in Paris, France
landmarks.summary: The Eiffel Tower is a lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. It is named after the engineer Gustave Eiffel, whose company designed and built the tower from 1887 to 1889.

landmarks.name: Great Wall of China
landmarks.description: Series of fortifications in northern China
landmarks.summary: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications in China. They were built across the historical northern borders of ancient Chinese states and Imperial China as protection against various nomadic groups from the Eurasian Steppe. The first walls date to the 7th century BC; these were joined together in the Qin dynasty.

credit.author: Severin.stalder

landmarks.name: Mount Kilimanjaro
landmarks.description: Mountain in Tanzania, highest in Africa
landmarks.summary: Mount Kilimanjaro is a large dormant stratovolcano in Tanzania. It is the highest mountain in Africa and the highest free-standing mountain above sea level in the world, at 5,895 m (19,341 ft) above sea level and 4,900 m (16,100 ft) above its plateau base.

landmarks.name: Lake Baikal
landmarks.description: Freshwater rift lake in Russia
landmarks.summary: Lake Baikal is a rift lake and the deepest lake in the world. It is situated in southern Siberia, Russia, between the federal subjects of Irkutsk Oblast to the northwest and the Republic of Buryatia to the southeast.

credit.title: File:Baikal, Cape Burhan, Shaman Rock, Olkhon Island, Lake Baikal, Russia.jpg
credit.author: Vyacheslav Argenberg

landmarks.name: Statue of Liberty
landmarks.description: Colossal sculpture in New York Harbor
landmarks.summary: The Statue of Liberty is a colossal neoclassical sculpture of a robed and crowned woman located on Liberty Island, part of New York City, in New York Harbor.

credit.title: File:Front view of Statue of Liberty (cropped).jpg
credit.author: AskALotl

landmarks.name: Burj Khalifa
landmarks.description: Skyscraper in Dubai, United Arab Emirates
landmarks.summary: The Burj Khalifa is a megatall skyscraper in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. 8 m and a roof height of 828 m (2,717 ft). It has been the tallest building in the world since its complete inauguration in 2011, surpassing Taipei 101, which had held the record since 2004.

landmarks.name: Colosseum
landmarks.description: Ancient Roman amphitheater in Rome
landmarks.summary: The Colosseum is an elliptical amphitheatre in the centre of the city of Rome, Italy, just east of the Roman Forum. It is the largest ancient amphitheatre ever built, and is the largest standing amphitheatre in the world. Construction began under Emperor Vespasian in 72 and was completed in AD 80 under his successor and heir, Titus.

landmarks.name: Panama Canal
landmarks.description: Shipping route across Central America
landmarks.summary: The Panama Canal is an artificial 82-kilometer (51-mile) waterway in Panama that connects the Caribbean Sea in the Atlantic Ocean with the Pacific Ocean. It cuts across the narrowest point of the Isthmus of Panama and is a conduit for maritime trade between the Atlantic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean.

credit.author: Adam Jones

landmarks.name: Hagia Sophia
landmarks.description: Mosque and former church in Istanbul, Turkey
landmarks.summary: Hagia Sophia, officially the Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque, is a mosque and a major cultural and historical site in Istanbul, Turkey. It was formerly a church (360–1453) and a museum (1935–2020).

credit.title: File:Hagia Sophia (228968325).jpeg
credit.author: Adli Wahid

landmarks.name: Louvre
landmarks.description: Art museum in Paris, France
landmarks.summary: The Louvre is a national art museum in Paris, France. It is located on the Right Bank of the Seine in the city's 1st arrondissement (district) and home to some of the most canonical works of Western art, including the Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and Winged Victory.

landmarks.name: Machu Picchu
landmarks.description: 15th-century Inca citadel in Peru
landmarks.summary: Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca citadel located in the Eastern Cordillera of southern Peru on a mountain ridge at 2,430 meters (7,970 ft).

landmarks.name: Kaaba
landmarks.description: Building at the center of Masjid al-Haram
landmarks.summary: The Kaaba, also spelled Kaʽba, Kaʽbah or Kabah, sometimes referred to as al-Kaʽba al-Musharrafa, is a stone building at the center of Islam's most important mosque and holiest site, the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. It is considered by Muslims to be the Baytullah and determines the qibla for Muslims around the world.

credit.title: File:The Ka'ba, Great Mosque of Mecca, Saudi Arabia (4).jpg
credit.author: Richard Mortel

landmarks.name: White House
landmarks.description: Residence and workplace of the US president
landmarks.summary: The White House is the official residence and workplace of the president of the United States. S. president since John Adams in 1800 when the national capital was moved from Philadelphia. The White House is also a metonym for the Executive Office of the President.

landmarks.name: Dead Sea
landmarks.description: Salt lake in the Levant
landmarks.summary: The Dead Sea, also known by other names, is a landlocked salt lake bordered by Jordan to the east, the West Bank to the west and Israel to the southwest. It lies in the endorheic basin of the Jordan Rift Valley, and its main tributary is the Jordan River.

landmarks.name: Sagrada Família
landmarks.description: Basilica under construction since 1882 in Barcelona, Spain
landmarks.summary: Basílica i Temple Expiatori de la Sagrada Família, or simply Sagrada Família, is a Catholic Basilica under construction in the Eixample district of Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain. Designed by the Spanish architect Antoni Gaudí, it is the tallest church in the world.

landmarks.name: Angkor Wat
landmarks.description: Buddhist temple complex in Cambodia
landmarks.summary: Angkor Wat is a Theravada Buddhist temple complex, originally built as a Vaishnava Hindu temple, in Siem Reap, Cambodia. It is the largest religious complex in the world.

landmarks.name: Empire State Building
landmarks.description: Office skyscraper in Manhattan, New York
landmarks.summary: The Empire State Building is a 102-story, supertall skyscraper in the Midtown South neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, United States. The building was designed in the Art Deco style by Shreve, Lamb & Harmon and constructed between 1930 and 1931. Its name is derived from "Empire State", the nickname of New York state.

landmarks.name: Stonehenge
landmarks.description: Prehistoric monument in England
landmarks.summary: Stonehenge is a prehistoric megalithic structure on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, England, two miles (3 km) west of Amesbury. 1 m) wide, and weighing around 25 tons, topped by connecting horizontal lintel stones which are held in place with mortise and tenon joints—a feature unique among contemporary monuments.

landmarks.name: Mount Fuji
landmarks.description: Volcano in Japan
landmarks.summary: 24 m. It is the highest mountain in Japan, the second-highest volcano on any Asian island, and the seventh-highest peak of an island on Earth. Mount Fuji last erupted from 1707 to 1708.

credit.author: Suicasmo

landmarks.name: St. Peter's Basilica
landmarks.description: Roman Catholic basilica and landmark in Vatican City
landmarks.summary: The Papal Basilica of Saint Peter in the Vatican, or simply St. Peter's Basilica, is a church of the Italian Renaissance located in Vatican City, an independent microstate enclaved within the city of Rome, Italy. It was initially planned in the 15th century by Pope Nicholas V and then Pope Julius II to replace the ageing Old St.

credit.title: File:Basilica di San Pietro in Vaticano September 2015-1a.jpg
credit.author: Alvesgaspar

landmarks.name: Great Barrier Reef
landmarks.description: Coral reef system in Queensland, Australia
landmarks.summary: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, composed of over 2,900 individual reefs and 900 islands stretching for over 2,300 kilometres (1,400 mi) over an area of approximately 344,400 square kilometres (133,000 mi2). The reef is located in the Coral Sea, off the coast of Queensland, Australia.

credit.title: File:Aerial View of Great Barrier Reef (Ank Kumar) 02.jpg
credit.author: Ank Kumar

landmarks.name: Pompeii
landmarks.description: Ancient city near modern Naples, Italy
landmarks.summary: Pompeii was a city in what is now the municipality of Pompei, near Naples, in the Campania region of Italy. Along with Herculaneum, Stabiae, and many surrounding villas, it was buried under 4 to 6 m of volcanic ash and pumice in the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD.

landmarks.name: Niagara Falls
landmarks.description: Waterfalls between the United States and Canada
landmarks.summary: S. state of New York. The largest of the three is Horseshoe Falls, which straddles the international border of the two countries. It is also known as the Canadian Falls. The smaller American Falls and Bridal Veil Falls lie within the United States.

landmarks.name: Galápagos Islands
landmarks.description: Ecuadorian volcanic archipelago
landmarks.summary: The Galápagos Islands are an archipelago of volcanic islands in the Eastern Pacific, located around the equator, 485 nautical miles west of the mainland of South America. They form the Galápagos Province of the Republic of Ecuador, with a population of slightly over 33,450 in 2020.

landmarks.name: Mount Rushmore
landmarks.description: Mountain with U.S. presidential sculptures
landmarks.summary: The Mount Rushmore National Memorial is a national memorial featuring a colossal sculpture carved into the granite face of Mount Rushmore in the Black Hills, about 2 mi (3 km) southwest of Keystone, South Dakota, United States.

landmarks.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
landmarks.description: Cathedral in Paris, France, built 1163–1345
landmarks.summary: Notre-Dame de Paris, often referred to simply as Notre-Dame, is a medieval Catholic cathedral and basilica on the Île de la Cité, in the 4th arrondissement of Paris, France. It is the cathedral church of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Paris.

landmarks.name: Petra
landmarks.description: Ancient rock-cut historical city in Jordan
landmarks.summary: Petra is an ancient city and archaeological site in southern Jordan. Famous for its rock-cut architecture and water conduit systems, Petra is also called the "Rose City" because of the colour of the sandstone from which it is carved. The city is one of the New 7 Wonders of the World and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

landmarks.name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
landmarks.description: Bell tower in Pisa, Italy
landmarks.summary: The Leaning Tower of Pisa, or simply the Tower of Pisa, is the campanile, or freestanding bell tower, of Pisa Cathedral. It is known for its nearly four-degree lean, the result of an unstable foundation. The tower is one of three structures in Pisa's Cathedral Square, which includes the cathedral and Pisa Baptistry.

landmarks.name: Palace of Versailles
landmarks.description: Former royal residence in Versailles, France
landmarks.summary: The Palace of Versailles is a château and historic monument in Versailles in the Yvelines department of France, southwest of Paris. It served as the principal residence of the French kings Louis XIV, Louis XV, and Louis XVI.

landmarks.name: Golden Gate Bridge
landmarks.description: Bridge in the San Francisco Bay Area
landmarks.summary: 6 km) strait connecting San Francisco Bay and the Pacific Ocean in California, United States. S. Route 101 and California State Route 1 across the strait. S. Bicycle Route 95.

landmarks.name: Mont Blanc
landmarks.description: Highest mountain in the Alps (4,806.m)
landmarks.summary: 9 ft) above sea level, located right at the Franco-Italian border. It is the highest mountain in Europe outside the Caucasus Mountains, the second-most prominent mountain in Europe, and the 11th most prominent mountain in the world.

landmarks.name: Mount Etna
landmarks.description: Active volcano on the east coast of Sicily, Italy
landmarks.summary: Mount Etna, or simply Etna, is an active stratovolcano on the east coast of Sicily, Italy, in the Metropolitan City of Catania, between the cities of Messina and Catania. It is located above the convergent plate margin between the African Plate and the Eurasian Plate.

landmarks.name: Grand Canyon
landmarks.description: Steep-sided canyon in Arizona, US
landmarks.summary: The Grand Canyon is a steep-sided canyon carved by the Colorado River in Arizona, United States. The Grand Canyon is 277 miles (446 km) long, up to 18 miles (29 km) wide and attains a depth of over a mile.

credit.author: Lennart Sikkema

landmarks.name: Denali
landmarks.description: Highest mountain in North America
landmarks.summary: Denali, federally designated as Mount McKinley, is the highest mountain peak in North America, with a summit elevation of 20,310 feet (6,190 m) above sea level. Its vertical relief above the surrounding plateaus is one of the greatest on Earth, measuring about 18,000 feet.

landmarks.name: Forbidden City
landmarks.description: Imperial palace complex in Beijing, China
landmarks.summary: The Forbidden City is the imperial palace complex in the center of the Imperial City in Beijing, China. It was the residence of twenty-four Ming and Qing dynasty Emperors and was the center of political power in China from 1420 to 1924.

landmarks.name: Taipei 101
landmarks.description: Skyscraper in Taiwan
landmarks.summary: Taipei 101, formerly known as the Taipei World Financial Center, is a 508-meter, 101-story skyscraper in Taipei, Taiwan. It is owned by the Taipei Financial Center Corporation. It was officially classified as the world's tallest building from its opening on 31 December 2004 until it was surpassed by the Burj Khalifa in 2009.

landmarks.name: Lake Titicaca
landmarks.description: Large lake on the border of Peru and Bolivia
landmarks.summary: Lake Titicaca is a large lake in the Andes mountains on the border of Bolivia and Peru. It is often called the highest navigable lake in the world. It is often listed as a freshwater lake, though its waters are slightly brackish. Titicaca is the largest lake in South America, both in terms of the volume of water and surface area.

credit.author: Didier Moïse

landmarks.name: Chichén Itzá
landmarks.description: Pre-Columbian Maya city in Mexico
landmarks.summary: Chichen Itza was a large pre-Columbian city built by the Maya people of the Terminal Classic period. The archeological site is located in Tinúm Municipality, Yucatán, Mexico, between the cities of Valladolid and Mérida.

landmarks.name: Christ the Redeemer
landmarks.description: Colossal statue in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
landmarks.summary: Christ the Redeemer is an Art Deco statue of Jesus in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, created by French-Polish sculptor Paul Landowski and built by Brazilian engineer Heitor da Silva Costa, in collaboration with French engineer Albert Caquot and Romanian sculptor Gheorghe Leonida who sculpted the face.

landmarks.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
landmarks.description: Palace in Bavaria, Germany
landmarks.summary: Neuschwanstein Castle is a 19th-century historicist palace on a rugged hill of the foothills of the Alps in the very south of Germany, near the border with Austria.

landmarks.name: Terracotta Army
landmarks.description: Collection of ancient Chinese military statues
landmarks.summary: The Terracotta Army is a collection of terracotta sculptures depicting the armies of Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor of China. It is a form of funerary art buried with the emperor in 210–209 BCE in his mausoleum with the purpose of protecting him in his afterlife.

landmarks.name: Mont-Saint-Michel
landmarks.description: Tidal island in Normandy, France
landmarks.summary: Mont-Saint-Michel is a tidal island and mainland commune in Normandy, France.

landmarks.name: Buckingham Palace
landmarks.description: Administrative headquarters of the British monarch
landmarks.summary: Buckingham Palace is the official residence and administrative headquarters of the monarch of the United Kingdom in London, England. Located in the City of Westminster, the palace is often at the centre of state occasions and royal hospitality. It has been a focal point for the British people at times of national rejoicing and mourning.

landmarks.name: Aconcagua
landmarks.description: Highest mountain in the Americas
landmarks.summary: Aconcagua is a mountain in the Principal Cordillera of the Andes range, located in Mendoza Province, Argentina. 15 metres, it is the highest mountain outside Asia. It is the second-most topographically prominent peak in the world and one of the Seven Summits, the highest mountains on each of the seven continents.

landmarks.name: Pantheon, Rome
landmarks.description: Roman temple, later church, in Rome
landmarks.summary: The Pantheon is an ancient Polytheist temple in Rome, Italy, originally built under Roman emperor Augustus and reconstructed under Hadrian (117–138).

landmarks.name: Cologne Cathedral
landmarks.description: Historic church in Cologne, Germany
landmarks.summary: Cologne Cathedral is a Catholic cathedral in Cologne, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is the seat of the Archbishop of Cologne and of the administration of the Archdiocese of Cologne. It is a renowned monument of German Catholicism and Gothic architecture and was declared a World Heritage Site in 1996.

landmarks.name: Acropolis of Athens
landmarks.description: Ancient citadel above the city of Athens
landmarks.summary: The Acropolis of Athens is an ancient citadel located on a rocky outcrop above the city of Athens, Greece, and contains the remains of several ancient buildings of great architectural and historical significance, the most famous being the Parthenon.

credit.title: File:1029 Acropolis of Athens in Greece at night Photo by Giles Laurent.jpg
credit.author: Giles Laurent

landmarks.name: Alhambra
landmarks.description: Palace and fortress complex in Granada, Spain
landmarks.summary: The Alhambra is a palace and fortress complex located in Granada, Spain. It is one of the most famous monuments of Islamic architecture and the only well-preserved palace from the medieval Islamic world. Additionally, the palace contains notable examples of Spanish Renaissance architecture.

credit.author: Jebulon

landmarks.name: Big Ben
landmarks.description: Clock tower in London, England
landmarks.summary: Big Ben is the nickname for the Great Bell of the Great Clock of Westminster, and, by extension, for the clock tower that stands at the north end of the Palace of Westminster in London, England. Originally named the Clock Tower, the structure was renamed the Elizabeth Tower in 2012 to mark the Diamond Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II.

credit.author: Christian David

landmarks.name: Dubrovnik Old Town
landmarks.description: Coastal city in southern Croatia
landmarks.summary: Dubrovnik, historically also known as Ragusa, is a city in southern Dalmatia, Croatia, by the Adriatic Sea. It is one of the most prominent tourist destinations in the Mediterranean, a seaport and the centre of the Dubrovnik-Neretva County. In 2021, its total population was 41,562.

credit.author: Zysko serhii

landmarks.name: Persepolis
landmarks.description: Ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire
landmarks.summary: Persepolis was the ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire. It is situated in the plains of Marvdasht, encircled by the southern Zagros Mountains, Fars province of Iran. It is one of the key Iranian cultural heritage sites and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

credit.title: File:2018-09-21 Iran, Persepolis, Tachara (from the southeast).jpg
credit.author: Laurens R. Krol

landmarks.name: Arc de Triomphe
landmarks.description: Triumphal arch in Paris, France
landmarks.summary: The Arc de Triomphe de l'Étoile, often simply called the Arc de Triomphe, is one of the most famous monuments in Paris, France.

landmarks.name: Socotra
landmarks.description: Largest of four islands of the Socotra Archipelago, Yemen
landmarks.summary: Socotra locally known as Saqatri, is an island in the Indian Ocean that is part of a Yemen. It is situated between the Gulf of Aden, the Guardafui Channel and the Arabian Sea, and lies near major shipping routes. The largest of the six islands in the Socotra archipelago, it comprises around 95% of the landmass of the archipelago.

landmarks.name: Sydney Opera House
landmarks.description: Performing arts centre in Australia
landmarks.summary: The Sydney Opera House is a multi-venue performing arts centre in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia. Located on the foreshore of Sydney Harbour, it is widely regarded as one of the world's most famous and distinctive buildings, and a masterpiece of 20th-century architecture.

landmarks.name: Dome of the Rock
landmarks.description: Islamic building in Al-Aqsa, Jerusalem
landmarks.summary: The Dome of the Rock is an octagonal Islamic shrine at the center of the Al-Aqsa mosque compound on the Temple Mount in the Old City of Jerusalem.

landmarks.name: Uluru
landmarks.description: Sandstone monolith in the Northern Territory, Australia
landmarks.summary: Uluru, also known as Ayers Rock and officially gazetted as Uluru / Ayers Rock, is a large sandstone monolith. It crops out near the centre of Australia in the southern part of the Northern Territory, 335 km (208 mi) south-west of Alice Springs.

landmarks.name: Victoria Falls
landmarks.description: Waterfall on the Zambezi River in Zambia and Zimbabwe
landmarks.summary: Victoria Falls is a waterfall on the Zambezi River, located on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe. It is one of the world's largest waterfalls, with a width of 1,708 m (5,604 ft). The region around it has a high degree of biodiversity in both plants and animals.

landmarks.name: Ephesus
landmarks.description: Ancient Greek city in Anatolia
landmarks.summary: Ephesus was an ancient Greek city on the coast of Ionia, in present-day Selçuk in İzmir Province, Turkey. It was built in the 10th century BC on the site of Apasa, a city-state that was also the capital of Arzawa, by Attic and Ionian Greek colonists.

landmarks.name: Petronas Towers
landmarks.description: Interlinked supertall skyscraper in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
landmarks.summary: 9 m (1,483 ft). From 1998 to 2004, they were the tallest buildings in the world until they were surpassed by the Taipei 101 skyscraper in Taiwan.

landmarks.name: Windsor Castle
landmarks.description: Official country residence of British monarch
landmarks.summary: Windsor Castle is a royal residence at Windsor in the English county of Berkshire, about 25 miles (40 km) west of central London. It is strongly associated with the English and succeeding British royal family, and embodies almost a millennium of architectural history.

landmarks.name: Cappadocia
landmarks.description: Historical region in Central Anatolia, Turkey
landmarks.summary: Cappadocia is a historical region in Central Anatolia region, Turkey. It is largely in the provinces of Nevşehir, Kayseri, Aksaray, Kırşehir, Sivas and Niğde. Today, the touristic Cappadocia Region is located in Nevşehir province.

landmarks.name: Cartagena Old Town
landmarks.description: City in coastal northern Colombia
landmarks.summary: Cartagena, known since the imperial era as Cartagena de Indias, is a city and one of the major ports on the northern coast of Colombia in the Caribbean Coast Region, along the Caribbean Sea.

landmarks.name: Cape of Good Hope
landmarks.description: Headland of Cape Peninsula, South Africa
landmarks.summary: The Cape of Good Hope ; Portuguese: Cabo da Boa Esperança ) is a rocky headland on the Atlantic coast of the Cape Peninsula in South Africa.

credit.author: August Dominus

landmarks.name: Matterhorn
landmarks.description: Mountain in the Swiss and Italian Alps
landmarks.summary: The Matterhorn is a mountain of the Alps, straddling the main watershed and border between Switzerland and Italy. It is a large, near-symmetric pyramidal peak in the extended Monte Rosa area of the Pennine Alps, whose summit is 4,478 metres (14,692 ft) above sea level, making it one of the highest summits in the Alps and Europe.

landmarks.name: Golden Temple
landmarks.description: Sikh religious site in Punjab, India
landmarks.summary: The Golden Temple is a gurdwara located in Amritsar, Punjab, India. It is the pre-eminent spiritual site of Sikhism and its holiest site. The gurdwara complex is a collection of buildings around the sanctum sanctorum and the sarovar, known as the Amrit Sarovar.

landmarks.name: Brooklyn Bridge
landmarks.description: Bridge in New York City
landmarks.summary: The Brooklyn Bridge is a cable-stayed suspension bridge in New York City, spanning the East River between the boroughs of Manhattan and Brooklyn. Opened on May 24, 1883, the Brooklyn Bridge was the first fixed crossing of the East River. 7 m) above mean high water.

landmarks.name: Central Park
landmarks.description: Public park in Manhattan, New York
landmarks.summary: Central Park is an urban park between the Upper West Side and Upper East Side neighborhoods of Manhattan in New York City, and the first landscaped park in the United States.

credit.author: Anthony Quintano from Hillsborough, NJ, United States
credit.credit: Global Citizen Festival Central Park New York City from NYonAir

landmarks.name: CN Tower
landmarks.description: Communications and observation tower in Toronto, Canada
landmarks.summary: 3 ft) communications and observation tower in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Completed in 1976, it is located in downtown Toronto, built on the former Railway Lands. Its name "CN" refers to Canadian National, the railway company that built the tower.

credit.author: Maksim Sokolov (maxergon.com)

landmarks.name: Moai of Easter Island
landmarks.description: Monolithic statues on Easter Island
landmarks.summary: Moai or moꞌai are monolithic human figures carved from stone by the Rapa Nui people, on Rapa Nui in eastern Polynesia between the years 1250 and 1500. Nearly half are still at Rano Raraku, the main moai quarry, but hundreds were transported from there and set on stone platforms called ahu around the island's perimeter.

credit.author: Ian Sewell
credit.credit: IanAndWendy.com Photo gallery from Easter Island

landmarks.name: Iguazu Falls
landmarks.description: Waterfalls on the Iguazú River on the border of Argentina and Brazil
landmarks.summary: The Iguazú Falls or Iguaçu Falls are waterfalls of the Iguazu River on the border of the Argentine province of Misiones and the Brazilian state of Paraná. Together, they make up the largest waterfall system in the world. The falls divide the river into the upper and lower Iguazu.

landmarks.name: St Paul's Cathedral
landmarks.description: Anglican cathedral in London, England
landmarks.summary: St Paul's Cathedral, formally the Cathedral Church of St Paul in London, is an Anglican cathedral in London, England, the seat of the bishop of London. The cathedral serves as the mother church of the Diocese of London in the Church of England. It is on Ludgate Hill at the highest point of the City of London.

landmarks.name: Tower Bridge
landmarks.description: Bridge over the Thames in London, England
landmarks.summary: Tower Bridge is a Grade I listed combined bascule, suspension, and, until 1960, cantilever bridge in London, built between 1886 and 1894, designed by Horace Jones and engineered by John Wolfe Barry with the help of Henry Marc Brunel.

landmarks.name: Mount Sinai
landmarks.description: Mountain in the Sinai Peninsula
landmarks.summary: Mount Sinai, also known as Jabal Musa, is a mountain on the Sinai Peninsula of Egypt. It is one of several locations claimed to be the biblical Mount Sinai, the place where, according to the sacred scriptures of the three major Abrahamic religions, the Hebrew prophet Moses received the Ten Commandments from God.

landmarks.name: Teotihuacan
landmarks.description: Ancient Mesoamerican city
landmarks.summary: Teotihuacan is an ancient Mesoamerican city located in a sub-valley of the Valley of Mexico, which is located in the State of Mexico, 40 kilometers (25 mi) northeast of modern-day Mexico City.

credit.title: File:ZA77 Teotihuacán edo de mex Herberto de la rosa.jpg
credit.author: Hdlrosa

landmarks.name: Pyramids of Giza
landmarks.description: Archaeological site near Cairo, Egypt
landmarks.summary: The Giza pyramid complex in Egypt is home to the Great Pyramid, the pyramid of Khafre, and the pyramid of Menkaure, along with their associated pyramid complexes and the Great Sphinx. All were built during the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom of ancient Egypt, between c. 2600 – c. 2500 BC.

landmarks.name: Brandenburg Gate
landmarks.description: Triumphal arch and gate in Berlin, Germany
landmarks.summary: The Brandenburg Gate is an 18th-century neoclassical monument in Berlin, Germany. One of the best-known landmarks of the country, it was erected on the site of a former city gate that marked the start of the road from Berlin to Brandenburg an der Havel, the former capital of the Margraviate of Brandenburg.

landmarks.name: Palmyra
landmarks.description: Ancient city in central Syria
landmarks.summary: Palmyra is an ancient city in central Syria. Located in the eastern part of the Levant, archaeological finds around the site date back to the Neolithic period, and documents first mention the city in the early second millennium BC.

landmarks.name: United States Capitol
landmarks.description: Meeting place of the United States Congress
landmarks.summary: The United States Capitol, often called the Capitol or the Capitol Building, is the seat of the United States Congress, the legislative branch of the federal government. C. S. Capitol forms the origin point for the street-numbering system of the district as well as its four quadrants.

landmarks.name: Hoover Dam
landmarks.description: Dam in Nevada and Arizona, US
landmarks.summary: S. states of Nevada and Arizona. Constructed between 1931 and 1936, during the Great Depression, it was dedicated on September 30, 1935, by President Franklin D. Roosevelt. Its construction was the result of a massive effort involving thousands of workers, and cost over 96 lives.

landmarks.name: Angel Falls
landmarks.description: Tallest single drop waterfall in the world, Venezuela
landmarks.summary: Angel Falls is a waterfall in Venezuela. It is the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall, with a height of 979 metres (3,212 ft), and a plunge of 807 m (2,648 ft). The waterfall drops over the edge of the Auyán-tepui mountain in the Canaima National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Gran Sabana region of Bolívar State.

landmarks.name: Santorini
landmarks.description: Greek island in the Aegean Sea
landmarks.summary: Santorini, officially Thira or Thera, is a Greek island in the southern Aegean Sea, about 200 km (120 mi) southeast from the mainland. It is the largest island of a small, circular archipelago formed by the Santorini caldera.

credit.title: File:1000 Three domes of Oia in Santorini Photo by Giles Laurent.jpg
credit.author: Giles Laurent

landmarks.name: Milan Cathedral
landmarks.description: Cathedral church of Milan, Italy
landmarks.summary: Milan Cathedral, or Metropolitan Cathedral-Basilica of the Nativity of Saint Mary, is the cathedral church of Milan, Lombardy, Italy. Dedicated to the Nativity of St. Mary, it is the seat of the Archbishop of Milan, currently Archbishop Mario Delpini.

credit.title: File:Milan Cathedral from Piazza del Duomo.jpg
credit.author: Jiuguang Wang

landmarks.name: Trevi Fountain
landmarks.description: Fountain in Rome, Italy
landmarks.summary: The Trevi Fountain is an 18th-century fountain in the Trevi district in Rome, Italy, designed by Italian architect Nicola Salvi and completed by Giuseppe Pannini in 1762. 3 ft) wide, it is the largest Baroque fountain in the world and one of the most famous fountains in the world.

landmarks.name: Blue Mosque
landmarks.description: 17th-century mosque in Turkey
landmarks.summary: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque, popularly known as the Blue Mosque, is an Ottoman-era historical imperial mosque located in Istanbul, Turkey. It was constructed between 1609 and 1617 during the rule of Ahmed I. It attracts a large number of tourists and is one of the most iconic and popular monuments of Ottoman architecture.

credit.title: File:Istanbul (34223582516) (cropped).jpg
credit.author: Pedro Szekely from Los Angeles, USA

landmarks.name: Borobudur
landmarks.description: 9th-century Buddhist temple in Java, Indonesia
landmarks.summary: Borobudur, also transcribed Barabudur, is a 9th-century Mahayana Buddhist temple in Magelang Regency, near the town of Muntilan, northwest of the city of Yogyakarta, in Central Java, Indonesia.

landmarks.name: Red Fort
landmarks.description: Historical Mughal fort in Delhi, India
landmarks.summary: The Red Fort is a historic Mughal fort located in the Old Delhi area of Delhi, India. Serving as the main residence of the Mughal emperors, it was commissioned by Emperor Shah Jahan on the 12th of May 1639; the fort was constructed following his decision to shift the Mughal capital from Agra to Delhi.

landmarks.name: Washington Monument
landmarks.description: U.S. national memorial in Washington, D.C.
landmarks.summary: , built to commemorate George Washington, a Founding Father of the United States and the nation's first president. Standing east of the Reflecting Pool and the Lincoln Memorial, the monument is made of bluestone gneiss for the foundation and of granite for the construction.

landmarks.name: Times Square
landmarks.description: Intersection and area in Manhattan, New York
landmarks.summary: Times Square is one of the world's busiest pedestrian intersections, tourist destinations, and entertainment hubs. It is formed by the junction of Broadway, Seventh Avenue, and 42nd Street in Midtown Manhattan, New York City.

landmarks.name: Abu Simbel
landmarks.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site in southern Egypt
landmarks.summary: Abu Simbel is a historic site comprising two massive rock-cut temples in the village of Abu Simbel, Aswan Governorate, Upper Egypt, near the border with Sudan. It is located on the western bank of Lake Nasser, about 230 km (140 mi) southwest of Aswan.

landmarks.name: Lake Como
landmarks.description: Lake in Lombardy, Italy
landmarks.summary: Lake Como, also known as Lario, is a lake of glacial origin in Lombardy, Italy. It has an area of 146 km2 (56 sq mi), making it the third-largest lake in Italy, after Lake Garda and Lake Maggiore. At over 400 metres (1,300 ft) deep, it is one of the deepest lakes in Europe.

landmarks.name: Prophet's Mosque
landmarks.description: Historic mosque in Medina, Saudi Arabia
landmarks.summary: The Prophet's Mosque is the second mosque built by the Islamic prophet Muhammad in Medina, after the Quba Mosque, as well as the second largest mosque and holiest site in Islam, after the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, in the Saudi region of the Hejaz.

credit.title: File:Masjid Nabawi The Prophet's Mosque, Madina.jpg
credit.author: Muhammad Mahdi Karim

landmarks.name: Burj Al Arab
landmarks.description: Luxury hotel in Dubai, United Arab Emirates
landmarks.summary: The Jumeirah Burj Al Arab, commonly known as Burj Al Arab, is a luxury hotel in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Developed and managed by Jumeirah, it is one of the tallest hotels in the world, although 39% of its total height is made up of non-occupiable space.

credit.title: File:Burj Al Arab and Jumeirah Beach (9601659067).jpg
credit.author: Yacine Hary

landmarks.name: London Eye
landmarks.description: Observation wheel in London, England
landmarks.summary: The London Eye, originally the Millennium Wheel, is a cantilevered observation wheel on the South Bank of the River Thames in London. It is the world's tallest cantilevered observation wheel, and the most popular paid tourist attraction in the United Kingdom with more than three million visitors annually.

landmarks.name: Valley of the Kings
landmarks.description: Necropolis in ancient Egypt
landmarks.summary: The Valley of the Kings, also known as the Valley of the Gates of the Kings, is an area in Egypt where, for a period of nearly 500 years from the Eighteenth Dynasty to the Twentieth Dynasty, rock-cut tombs were excavated for pharaohs and powerful nobles under the New Kingdom of ancient Egypt.

credit.title: File:Luxor Valley of the Kings R01.jpg
credit.author: Marc Ryckaert

landmarks.name: Bora Bora
landmarks.description: Island in French Polynesia
landmarks.summary: Bora Bora is a French island group in the Leeward Islands, comprising the western part of the Society Islands of French Polynesia, an overseas collectivity of the French Republic in the South Pacific. 55 km2 (12 sq mi). The main island, located about 230 kilometres northwest of Papeete, is surrounded by a lagoon and a barrier reef.

landmarks.name: Loch Ness
landmarks.description: Lake in Scotland
landmarks.summary: Loch Ness is a large freshwater loch in the Scottish Highlands. It takes its name from the River Ness, which flows from the northern end. Loch Ness is best known for claimed sightings of the cryptozoological Loch Ness Monster, also known affectionately as "Nessie".

landmarks.name: Giant's Causeway
landmarks.description: Interlocking basalt columns in Northern Ireland
landmarks.summary: The Giant's Causeway is an area of approximately 40,000 interlocking basalt columns, the result of an ancient volcanic fissure eruption, part of the North Atlantic Igneous Province active in the region during the Paleogene period.

landmarks.name: Nazca Lines
landmarks.description: Geoglyphs in the Nazca Desert, Peru
landmarks.summary: The Nazca lines are a group of geoglyphs made in the soil of the Nazca Desert in southern Peru. The area was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1994. The lines were created between 500 BC and 500 AD by people making depressions or shallow incisions in the desert floor, removing pebbles and leaving different-colored dirt exposed.

credit.title: File:Líneas de Nazca, Nazca, Perú, 2015-07-29, DD 52.JPG
credit.author: Diego Delso

landmarks.name: Florence Cathedral
landmarks.description: Church in Tuscany, Italy
landmarks.summary: Florence Cathedral, formally the Cathedral of Saint Mary of the Flower, is the cathedral of the Catholic Archdiocese of Florence in Florence, Italy.

credit.title: File:Cattedrale di Santa Maria del Fiore – Il Duomo di Firenze.jpg
credit.author: Gary Campbell-Hall

landmarks.name: Saint Basil's Cathedral
landmarks.description: 1561 Orthodox church in Moscow, Russia
landmarks.summary: The Cathedral of Vasily the Blessed, commonly known as Saint Basil's Cathedral, is a Russian Orthodox church on Red Square in the historic centre of Moscow. It is one of the most popular cultural symbols of Russia.

landmarks.name: Maldives
landmarks.description: Island country in South Asia
landmarks.summary: The Maldives, officially the Republic of Maldives, and historically known as the Maldive Islands, is an archipelagic country in South Asia, located in the Indian Ocean, near the southeastern boundary of the Arabian Sea. The Maldives is located southwest of India and Sri Lanka, about 750 kilometres from the Asian continent's mainland.

landmarks.name: Potala Palace
landmarks.description: Fortress in Lhasa, Tibet
landmarks.summary: Potala Palace is a museum complex in Lhasa, the capital of the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. It was formerly the winter palace of the Dalai Lamas, and from 1649 until 1959 served as the Dalai Lamas' residence. The palace complex became a museum following the annexation of Tibet by the People's Republic of China.

landmarks.name: Alcatraz Island
landmarks.description: Island in San Francisco Bay, California, US
landmarks.summary: 25 miles offshore from San Francisco in San Francisco Bay, California, near the Golden Gate strait. The island was developed in the mid-19th century with facilities for a lighthouse, a military fortification, and a military prison. In 1934, the island was converted into a federal prison, Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary.

landmarks.name: Himeji Castle
landmarks.description: Japanese castle in Hyōgo Prefecture
landmarks.summary: Himeji Castle is a hilltop Japanese castle complex situated in Himeji, a city in Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan. The castle is regarded as the finest surviving example of prototypical Japanese castle architecture, comprising a network of 83 structures with advanced defensive systems from the feudal period.

landmarks.name: Winter Palace
landmarks.description: Former imperial palace in Saint Petersburg, Russia
landmarks.summary: The Winter Palace is a palace in Saint Petersburg that served as the official residence of the House of Romanov, the emperors of Russia, from 1732 to 1917. The palace and its precincts now house the Hermitage Museum. The floor area is 233,345 square metres. 2 hectares.

landmarks.name: Qutb Minar
landmarks.description: Minaret in the Mehrauli area of Delhi, India
landmarks.summary: The Qutb Minar, also spelled Qutub Minar and Qutab Minar, is a minaret and victory tower, built during the Delhi sultanate, and comprising the Qutb complex, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Mehrauli, South Delhi, India.

landmarks.name: Great Zimbabwe
landmarks.description: Ruins of an ancient/medieval city in southeast Zimbabwe
landmarks.summary: Great Zimbabwe was a city in the south-eastern hills of the modern country of Zimbabwe, near Masvingo. It was settled by ancestral Shona people from around 1000 AD, and served as the capital of the Kingdom of Great Zimbabwe from the 13th century.

credit.author: Andrew Moore from Johannesburg, South Africa

landmarks.description: Active volcano in Hawaii
landmarks.summary: Template:Infobox mountain

landmarks.name: Baalbek
landmarks.description: City in Baalbek-Hermel, Lebanon
landmarks.summary: Baalbek is a city located east of the Litani River in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley, about 67 km (42 mi) northeast of Beirut. It is the capital of Baalbek-Hermel Governorate. In 1998, the city had a population of 82,608.

landmarks.name: Bondi Beach
landmarks.description: Suburb of Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
landmarks.summary: Bondi Beach is a beach and the surrounding suburb in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia. Bondi Beach is located 7 kilometres east of the Sydney central business district, in the local government area of Waverley Council, in the Eastern Suburbs. In the 2021 Australian census it had a population of 11,513 residents. Its postcode is 2026.

landmarks.name: Hallstatt
landmarks.description: Town in Gmunden, Upper Austria
landmarks.summary: Hallstatt is a small town in the Gmunden District of the Austrian state of Upper Austria. Situated between the southwestern shore of Hallstätter See and the steep slopes of the Dachstein massif, the town lies in the Salzkammergut region, on the national road linking Salzburg and Graz.

landmarks.name: Ellora Caves
landmarks.description: Ancient cave temples in Maharashtra, India
landmarks.summary: The Ellora Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Aurangabad, India. It is one of the largest rock-cut cave complexes in the world, with artwork dating from AD 600–1000, including Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain caves.

credit.title: File:Kailasa Temple Cave 16 Hindu Cave Ellora Caves India - panoramio (4).jpg
credit.author: Hiroki Ogawa

landmarks.name: Sacré-Cœur
landmarks.description: Catholic basilica and landmark in Paris, France
landmarks.summary: The Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Montmartre, commonly known as Sacré-Cœur Basilica or simply Sacré-Cœur, is a Catholic church and minor basilica in Paris dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus.

landmarks.name: Mosque–Cathedral of Córdoba
landmarks.description: Cathedral and former mosque in Córdoba, Spain
landmarks.summary: The Mosque–Cathedral of Córdoba is the cathedral of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Córdoba in the Spanish region of Andalusia. Officially called the Cathedral of Our Lady of the Assumption, it is dedicated to the Assumption of Mary.

credit.title: File:Mezquita de Córdoba desde el aire (Córdoba, España).jpg
credit.author: Toni Castillo Quero

landmarks.name: Temple of Heaven
landmarks.description: Imperial complex of religious buildings in Beijing, China
landmarks.summary: The Temple of Heaven is a complex of imperial religious Confucian buildings situated in the southeastern part of central Beijing. The complex was visited by the Emperors of the Ming and then later restored by the Qing dynasties for annual ceremonies of prayer to Heaven for a good harvest and other seasonal rites.

landmarks.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
landmarks.description: Bridge across Sydney Harbour in Australia
landmarks.summary: The Sydney Harbour Bridge is a steel through arch bridge in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia, spanning Sydney Harbour from the central business district (CBD) to the North Shore. The view of the bridge, the harbour, and the nearby Sydney Opera House is widely regarded as an iconic image of Sydney, and of Australia itself.

landmarks.name: Schönbrunn Palace
landmarks.description: Palace in Vienna, Austria
landmarks.summary: Schönbrunn Palace was the main summer residence of the Habsburg rulers, located in Hietzing, the 13th district of Vienna. The name Schönbrunn has its roots in an artesian well from which water was consumed by the court.

landmarks.name: Sigiriya
landmarks.description: Ancient rock fortress near Dambulla, Sri Lanka
landmarks.summary: Sigiriya or Sinhagiri is an ancient rock fortress located in the northern Matale District near the town of Dambulla in the Central Province, Sri Lanka. It is a site of historical and archaeological significance that is dominated by a massive column of granite approximately 180 m (590 ft) high.

credit.title: File:Sigiriya (141688197).jpeg
credit.author: Wrobell
credit.credit: Imported from 500px ( archived version ) by the Archive Team . ( detail page )

landmarks.name: Darvaza Gas Crater
landmarks.description: Burning natural gas field in Turkmenistan
landmarks.summary: The Darvaza gas crater, also known as the Door to Hell or Gates of Hell, and known officially as the Shining of Karakum, is a burning natural gas field collapsed into a cavern near Darvaza, Turkmenistan. Hundreds of natural gas fires illuminate the floor and rim of the crater. The gas crater has been burning since 1971.

landmarks.name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
landmarks.description: Modern and contemporary art museum in Bilbao, Spain
landmarks.summary: The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao is a museum of modern and contemporary art in Bilbao, Biscay, Spain. It is one of several museums affiliated to the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation and features permanent and visiting exhibits of works by Spanish and international artists.

landmarks.name: Cinque Terre
landmarks.description: Rugged portion of coast on the Italian Riviera, Liguria
landmarks.summary: The Cinque Terre is a coastal area within Liguria, in the northwest of Italy. It lies in the west of La Spezia Province, and comprises five villages: Monterosso al Mare, Vernazza, Corniglia, Manarola and Riomaggiore.

landmarks.name: Masada
landmarks.description: Ancient hilltop fortification in Israel
landmarks.summary: Masada is a mountain-top fortress complex in the Judaean Desert, overlooking the western shore of the Dead Sea in southeastern Israel. The fort, built in the first century BC, was constructed atop a natural plateau rising over 400 m (1,300 ft) above the surrounding terrain, 20 km (12 mi) east of modern Arad.

landmarks.name: Amalfi Coast
landmarks.description: Coastal area in the Campania region, Italy
landmarks.summary: The Amalfi Coast is a stretch of coastline overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea and the Gulf of Salerno. It is located in the Province of Salerno, in the Campania region of southern Italy, south of the Sorrentine Peninsula and north of the Cilentan Coast.

landmarks.name: Devils Tower
landmarks.description: Flat-topped volcanic plug in Wyoming, US
landmarks.summary: Devils Tower is a laccolithic butte, composed of igneous rock in the Bear Lodge Ranger District of the Black Hills, near Hulett and Sundance in Crook County, northeastern Wyoming, above the Belle Fourche River. It rises 1,267 feet (386 m) above the river, standing 867 ft (264 m) from summit to base.

credit.title: File:Columnar-jointed porphyritic phonolite (Eocene, 49 Ma; Devils Tower, Wyoming, USA) 48.jpg
credit.author: James St. John

landmarks.name: Crater Lake
landmarks.description: Caldera lake in Oregon, United States
landmarks.summary: Crater Lake is a volcanic crater lake in south-central Oregon in the Western United States. It is the main feature of Crater Lake National Park and is a tourist attraction known for its deep blue color and water clarity.

landmarks.name: Edinburgh Castle
landmarks.description: Historic castle in Edinburgh, Scotland
landmarks.summary: Edinburgh Castle is a historic castle in Edinburgh, Scotland. It stands on Castle Rock, which has been occupied by humans since at least the Iron Age. There has been a royal castle on the rock since the reign of Malcolm III in the 11th century, and the castle continued to be a royal residence until 1633.

credit.title: File:Edinburgh Castle from Princes Street Gardens (1).jpg
credit.author: Nilfanion

landmarks.name: Kiyomizu-dera
landmarks.description: Buddhist temple in Kyoto, Japan
landmarks.summary: Kiyomizu-dera is a Buddhist temple located in eastern Kyoto, Japan. It belongs to the Kita-Hosso sect of Japanese Buddhism and its honzon is a hibutsu statue of Jūichimen Kannon. The temple's full name is Otowa-san Kiyomizu-dera. The temple is the 16th stop on the Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage route.

landmarks.name: Ha Long Bay
landmarks.description: Bay in northern Vietnam
landmarks.summary: Hạ Long Bay or Halong Bay is a bay located in Northeastern Vietnam, administered by the city of Quảng Ninh. The name Hạ Long means "descending dragon". It features thousands of limestone karsts and islets in various shapes and sizes, for which it is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a popular travel destination.

landmarks.name: Tikal
landmarks.description: Ruin of ancient Maya city in Guatemala
landmarks.summary: Tikal is the ruin of an ancient city, which was likely to have been called Yax Mutal, found in a rainforest in Guatemala.

landmarks.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial
landmarks.description: Preserved ruins of the atomic bombing of Hiroshima, Japan
landmarks.summary: The Hiroshima Peace Memorial , originally the Hiroshima Prefectural Industrial Promotion Hall, and now commonly called the Genbaku Dome, Atomic Bomb Dome or A-Bomb Dome , is part of Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park in Hiroshima, Japan, and was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1996.

landmarks.name: Karnak
landmarks.description: Ancient Egyptian temple complex
landmarks.summary: The Karnak Temple Complex, commonly known as Karnak, comprises a vast mix of temples, pylons, chapels, and other buildings near Luxor, Egypt. Construction at the complex began during the reign of Senusret I in the Middle Kingdom and continued into the Ptolemaic Kingdom, although most of the extant buildings date from the New Kingdom.

landmarks.name: Meteora
landmarks.description: Rock formations and monasteries in Thessaly, Greece
landmarks.summary: Meteora is a rock formation in the regional unit of Trikala, in Thessaly, in northwestern Greece, hosting one of the most prominent complexes of Eastern Orthodox monasteries, viewed locally as second in importance only to Mount Athos. Their height is more than 20 metres (66 ft).

landmarks.name: Hawa Mahal
landmarks.description: Palace in Jaipur, Rajasthan, India
landmarks.summary: The Hawa Mahal is a palace in the city of Jaipur, Rajasthan, India. Built from red and pink sandstone, it is on the edge of the City Palace, Jaipur, and extends to the Zenana, or women's chambers.

credit.title: File:East facade Hawa Mahal Jaipur from ground level (July 2022) - img 01.jpg
credit.author: Chainwit.

landmarks.name: Lincoln Memorial
landmarks.description: National memorial in Washington, DC
landmarks.summary: S. C. The memorial is built in a neoclassical style in the form of a classical temple. The memorial's architect was Henry Bacon. In 1920, Daniel Chester French designed the large interior Abraham Lincoln statue, which was carved in marble by the Piccirilli brothers.

landmarks.name: Monument Valley
landmarks.description: Region of the Colorado Plateau, US
landmarks.summary: Monument Valley is a region of the Colorado Plateau characterized by a cluster of sandstone buttes, with the largest reaching 1,000 ft (300 m) above the valley floor. The most famous butte formations are located in northeastern Arizona along the Utah–Arizona state line.

landmarks.name: Table Mountain
landmarks.description: Mountain overlooking Cape Town, South Africa
landmarks.summary: Table Mountain is a flat-topped mountain forming a prominent landmark overlooking the city of Cape Town in South Africa.

credit.title: File:Table Mountain DanieVDM.jpg
credit.author: Danie van der Merwe from Cape Town, South Africa
credit.credit: View of Table Mountain from Bloubergstrand

landmarks.name: Gateway Arch
landmarks.description: US National Historic Landmark in St. Louis, Missouri
landmarks.summary: The Gateway Arch is a 630-foot-tall (192 m) monument in St. Louis, Missouri, United States. Clad in stainless steel and built in the form of a weighted catenary arch, it is the world's tallest arch and Missouri's tallest accessible structure. Some sources consider it the tallest human-made monument in the Western Hemisphere.

credit.author: St_Louis_night_expblend.jpg : Daniel Schwen derivative work: ← fetch comms

landmarks.name: Krak des Chevaliers
landmarks.description: Crusader castle near Homs, Syria
landmarks.summary: Krak des Chevaliers is a medieval castle in Syria and one of the most important preserved medieval castles in the world. The site was first inhabited in the 11th century by Kurdish troops garrisoned there by the Mirdasids. In 1142 it was given by Raymond II, Count of Tripoli, to the order of the Knights Hospitaller.

landmarks.name: Hampi
landmarks.description: Ancient and medieval monuments, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Karnataka, India
landmarks.summary: Hampi or Hampe, also referred to as the Group of Monuments at Hampi, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in the town of Hampi in Vijayanagara district, east-central Karnataka, India. Hampi predates the Vijayanagara Empire; it is mentioned in the Ramayana and the Puranas of Hinduism as Pampa Devi Tirtha Kshetra.

landmarks.name: Salar de Uyuni
landmarks.description: Salt flat in Bolivia
landmarks.summary: Salar de Uyuni is the largest salt flat in the world, with an area of approximately 10,582 square kilometres (4,086 mi2). It is situated in southwestern Bolivia, within the Daniel Campos Province of the Potosí Department, near the crest of the Andes Mountains, at an elevation of 3,656 m (11,995 ft) above sea level.

landmarks.name: Hollywood Sign
landmarks.description: Landmark in Los Angeles, California
landmarks.summary: The Hollywood Sign is an American landmark and cultural icon overlooking Hollywood, Los Angeles. Originally the Hollywoodland Sign, it is on Mount Lee, above Beachwood Canyon in the Santa Monica Mountains. 2 m) long. Due to increasing recognition, the sign was left up; the last four letters "LAND" were removed in 1949.

landmarks.name: Aoraki / Mount Cook
landmarks.description: Highest mountain in New Zealand
landmarks.summary: Aoraki / Mount Cook is the highest mountain in New Zealand. Its height, as of 2014, is listed as 3,724 metres. It is situated in the Southern Alps, the mountain range that runs the length of the South Island. A popular tourist destination, it is also a favourite challenge for mountaineers.

landmarks.name: Prambanan
landmarks.description: 9th-century Hindu temple compound near Yogyakarta, Indonesia
landmarks.summary: Prambanan is a 9th-century Hindu temple compound in the Special Region of Yogyakarta, in southern Java, Indonesia, dedicated to the Trimūrti, the expression of God as the Creator (Brahma), the Preserver (Vishnu), and the Destroyer (Shiva).

landmarks.name: Bran Castle
landmarks.description: Castle in Transylvania, Romania
landmarks.summary: Bran Castle is a castle in Bran, 25 kilometres (16 mi) southwest of Brașov. The castle was built by Saxons in 1377 who were given the privilege by Louis I of Hungary. It is a national monument and landmark in Transylvania. The fortress is on the Transylvanian side of the historical border with Wallachia, on road DN73.

landmarks.name: Itsukushima Shrine
landmarks.description: Shinto shrine in Hiroshima Prefecture, Japan
landmarks.summary: Itsukushima Shrine is a Shinto shrine on the island of Itsukushima, best known for its "floating" torii. It is in the city of Hatsukaichi, in Hiroshima Prefecture in Japan, accessible from the mainland by ferry at Miyajimaguchi Station.

landmarks.name: Space Needle
landmarks.description: Observation tower in Seattle, Washington, U.S.
landmarks.summary: The Space Needle is an observation tower in Seattle, Washington, United States. Considered to be an icon of the city, it has been designated a Seattle landmark. 3 million visitors.

landmarks.name: Las Vegas Strip
landmarks.description: Stretch of Las Vegas Boulevard with many resorts, shows, and casinos
landmarks.summary: The Las Vegas Strip is a stretch of Las Vegas Boulevard in Clark County, Nevada, that is known for its concentration of resort hotels and casinos. 8 km) long, and is immediately south of the Las Vegas city limits in the unincorporated towns of Paradise and Winchester, but is often referred to simply as "Las Vegas".

landmarks.description: Integrated resort in Singapore
landmarks.summary: Marina Bay Sands is an integrated resort fronting Marina Bay in Singapore and a landmark of the city. 88 billion).

landmarks.name: Rock of Gibraltar
landmarks.description: Monolithic limestone promontory located in the British overseas territory of Gibraltar
landmarks.summary: The Rock of Gibraltar is a monolithic limestone mountain 426 m (1,398 ft) high dominating the western entrance to the Mediterranean Sea at the Strait of Gibraltar. 6 mi) promontory stretching due south into the Mediterranean Sea and is located within the British territory of Gibraltar.

landmarks.name: Lotus Temple
landmarks.description: Baháʼí House of Worship in New Delhi, India
landmarks.summary: The Lotus Temple, also known as the Baháʼí House of Worship, New Delhi, is a Baháʼí House of Worship at Bahapur in south Delhi, India. Designed by the architect Fariborz Sahba, it takes the form of a half-open lotus of 27 free-standing marble-clad concrete petals, arranged in three rings of nine around a central hall.

landmarks.name: Osaka Castle
landmarks.description: Historic castle in the Chūō-ku ward of Osaka, Japan
landmarks.summary: Osaka Castle is a Japanese castle in Chūō-ku, Osaka, Japan. The castle is one of Japan's most famous landmarks and played a major role in the unification of Japan during the sixteenth century of the Azuchi–Momoyama period.

landmarks.name: Hungarian Parliament Building
landmarks.description: Seat of the National Assembly of Hungary
landmarks.summary: The Hungarian Parliament Building, also known as the Parliament of Budapest after its location, is the seat of the National Assembly of Hungary, a notable landmark of Hungary, and a popular tourist destination in Budapest. It is situated on Kossuth Square in the Pest side of the city, on the eastern bank of the Danube.

credit.title: File:Hungarian Parliament Building from across the Danube, 2025-01-11.jpg
credit.author: Kilyann Le Hen

landmarks.name: Stone Town, Zanzibar
landmarks.description: Old town of Zanzibar City, Tanzania
landmarks.summary: The Stone Town of Zanzibar, also known as Mji Mkongwe, is the old part of Zanzibar City, the main city of Zanzibar, in Tanzania. The newer portion of the city is known as Ng'ambo, Swahili for 'the other side'. Stone Town is located on the western coast of Unguja, the main island of the Zanzibar Archipelago.

landmarks.name: Belém Tower
landmarks.description: Fortified tower in Lisbon, Portugal
landmarks.summary: Belém Tower, officially the Tower of Saint Vincent, is a 16th-century fortification located in Lisbon, Portugal, which served as a point of embarkation and disembarkation for Portuguese explorers and as a ceremonial gateway to Lisbon. The tower symbolizes Portugal's maritime and colonial power in early modern Europe.

landmarks.name: Charles Bridge
landmarks.description: Medieval stone arch bridge across the Vltava river in Prague, Czechia
landmarks.summary: Charles Bridge is a medieval stone arch bridge that crosses the Vltava river in Prague, Czech Republic. Its construction started in 1357 under the auspices of King Charles IV, and finished in the early 15th century. The bridge replaced the old Judith Bridge built 1158–1172 that had been severely damaged by a flood in 1342.

credit.author: A.Savin

landmarks.name: Okavango Delta
landmarks.description: River delta in Botswana
landmarks.summary: The Okavango Delta or Okavango Grassland is a vast inland delta in Botswana formed where the Okavango River reaches a tectonic trough at an elevation of 930–1,000 m (3,050–3,280 ft) in the central part of the endorheic basin of the Kalahari Desert.

credit.title: File:Okavango Delta, Botswana1.jpg
credit.author: Joachim Huber
credit.credit: originally posted to Flickr as Okavango Delta, Botswana

landmarks.name: Zion National Park
landmarks.description: National park in Utah, United States
landmarks.summary: Zion National Park is a national park of the United States located in southwestern Utah near the town of Springdale. Located at the junction of the Colorado Plateau, Great Basin, and Mojave Desert regions, the park has a unique geography and a variety of life zones that allow for unusual plant and animal diversity.

landmarks.name: Pamukkale
landmarks.description: Natural site in Denizli Province in southwestern Turkey
landmarks.summary: Pamukkale, meaning "cotton castle" in Turkish, is a natural site in Denizli Province in southwestern Turkey. The area is famous for a carbonate mineral left by the flowing of thermal spring water. It is located in Turkey's Inner Aegean region, in the River Menderes valley, which has a temperate climate for most of the year.

landmarks.name: Aït Benhaddou
landmarks.description: Historical village in southeastern Morocco
landmarks.summary: Aït Benhaddou is a historic ighrem or ksar along the former caravan route between the Sahara and Marrakesh in Morocco. It is considered a great example of Moroccan earthen clay architecture and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.

credit.author: Petar Milošević

landmarks.name: Meenakshi Temple
landmarks.description: Historic Hindu temple in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India
landmarks.summary: Meenakshi Temple, also known as Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple, is a historic Hindu temple located on the southern bank of the Vaigai River in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India. It is dedicated to Meenakshi, a form of Parvati, and her consort Sundareswarar (Shiva).

landmarks.name: Summer Palace
landmarks.description: Complex of gardens and palaces in Beijing, China; UNESCO World Heritage Site
landmarks.summary: The Summer Palace or Yihe Garden consists of a vast ensemble of lakes, gardens and palaces located in Beijing. An imperial garden during the Qing dynasty, it includes Longevity Hill, Kunming Lake, and Seventeen-Arch Bridge. 1 sq mi), three-quarters of which is water.

credit.title: File:Longevity Hill of the Summer Palace.jpg
credit.author: xiquinhosilva

landmarks.name: Cotopaxi
landmarks.description: Active stratovolcano in Ecuador
landmarks.summary: 1 mi) south of Quito, and 31 km (19 mi) northeast of the city of Latacunga, Ecuador. It is the second highest summit in Ecuador, reaching a height of 5,897 m (19,347 ft). Cotopaxi is among the highest active volcanoes in the world.

landmarks.name: Leshan Giant Buddha
landmarks.description: Monumental sculpture
landmarks.summary: The Leshan Giant Buddha is a 71-meter (233 ft) tall stone statue, built between 712 and 804 AD. It is carved out of a cliff face of Cretaceous red bed sandstones that lies at the confluence of the Min River and Dadu River in the southern part of Sichuan Province in China, near the city of Leshan.

landmarks.name: Park Güell
landmarks.description: Public park system in Barcelona, Spain
landmarks.summary: Park Güell is a complex of parks and gardens in Barcelona with architectural elements, located in the La Salut neighborhood of the Gràcia district in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain. It is situated on the southern slope of the Turó del Carmel hill, part of the Collserola mountain range, overlooking the city.

landmarks.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
landmarks.description: Palace in Seoul, South Korea
landmarks.summary: Gyeongbokgung is a former royal palace in Seoul, South Korea. Established in 1395, it was the first royal palace of the Joseon dynasty, and is now one of the most significant tourist attractions in the country.

landmarks.name: Pont du Gard
landmarks.description: Ancient Roman aqueduct bridge
landmarks.summary: The Pont du Gard is an ancient Roman aqueduct bridge built in the first century AD to carry water over 50 km (31 mi) to the Roman colony of Nemausus (Nîmes). It crosses the river Gardon near the town of Vers-Pont-du-Gard in southern France. The Pont du Gard is one of the best preserved Roman aqueduct bridges.

landmarks.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
landmarks.description: Zen Buddhist temple in Kyoto, Japan
landmarks.summary: Kinkaku-ji , officially named Rokuon-ji , is a Zen Buddhist temple in Kyoto, Japan and a tourist attraction. It is designated as a World Heritage Site, a National Special Historic Site, a National Special Landscape, and one of the 17 Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto. 5 μm gold leaf.

landmarks.name: Mount Roraima
landmarks.description: Mountain in Brazil, Guyana and Venezuela
landmarks.summary: Mount Roraima is the highest of the Pacaraima chain of tepuis or plateaux in South America. It is located at the junction of Brazil, Guyana and Venezuela.

landmarks.name: Serengeti National Park
landmarks.description: National park in Tanzania
landmarks.summary: The Serengeti National Park is a large national park in northern Tanzania that stretches over 14,763 km2 (5,700 sq mi). It is located in eastern Mara Region and northeastern Simiyu Region and contains over 15,000 km2 (5,800 sq mi) of savanna. The park was established in 1940.

landmarks.name: Cliffs of Moher
landmarks.description: Sea cliffs in County Clare, Ireland
landmarks.summary: The Cliffs of Moher are sea cliffs located at the southwestern edge of the Burren region in County Clare, Ireland. They run for about 14 kilometres.

landmarks.name: Badshahi Mosque
landmarks.description: Mughal-era mosque in Lahore, Pakistan
landmarks.summary: The Badshahi Mosque is a Mughal-era imperial mosque located in Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan. It was constructed between 1671 and 1673 by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb, opposite to the Lahore Fort in the northern outskirts of the historic Walled City. It is widely considered to be an iconic landmark of the country.

landmarks.name: Bryce Canyon
landmarks.description: National park in Utah, United States
landmarks.summary: Bryce Canyon National Park is a national park of the United States located in southwestern Utah. The major feature of the park is Bryce Canyon, which, despite its name, is not a canyon but a collection of giant natural amphitheaters along the eastern side of the Paunsaugunt Plateau.

credit.title: File:Inspiration Point Bryce Canyon November 2018 panorama.jpg
credit.author: King of Hearts

landmarks.name: Château de Chambord
landmarks.description: Castle in Chambord, France
landmarks.summary: The Château de Chambord in Chambord, Centre-Val de Loire, France, is one of the most recognisable châteaux in the world because of its very distinctive French Renaissance architecture, which blends traditional French medieval forms with classical Renaissance structures.

credit.title: File:Aerial image of Château de Chambord (view from the southeast).jpg
credit.author: Carsten Steger

landmarks.name: Ziggurat of Ur
landmarks.description: Early Bronze Age ziggurat in present-day Iraq
landmarks.summary: The Ziggurat of Ur is a Neo-Sumerian ziggurat in what was the city of Ur near Nasiriyah, in present-day Dhi Qar Province, Iraq. The structure was built during the Early Bronze Age by King Ur-Nammu of the Third Dynasty of Ur.

landmarks.name: Kruger National Park
landmarks.description: First national park in South Africa
landmarks.summary: Kruger National Park is a national park in South Africa covering an area of 19,623 km2 (7,576 sq mi) in the provinces of Limpopo and Mpumalanga in the country's northeast. It extends 360 km (220 mi) from north to south and 65 km (40 mi) from east to west. The administrative headquarters are in Skukuza.

landmarks.name: Tulum
landmarks.description: Maya site in Quintana Roo, Mexico
landmarks.summary: Tulum is the site of a pre-Columbian Mayan walled city which served as a major port for Coba, in the Mexican state of Quintana Roo. The ruins are situated on 12-meter-tall (39 ft) cliffs along the east coast of the Yucatán Peninsula on the Caribbean Sea.

landmarks.name: Atomium
landmarks.description: Landmark building in Brussels, Belgium
landmarks.summary: The Atomium is a landmark modernist building in Brussels, Belgium, originally constructed as the centrepiece of the 1958 Brussels World's Fair.

landmarks.name: Great Blue Hole
landmarks.description: Marine sinkhole off the coast of Belize
landmarks.summary: The Great Blue Hole is a large marine sinkhole off the coast of Belize. It lies near the center of Lighthouse Reef, a small atoll 70 km (43 mi) from the mainland and Belize City. The hole is circular in shape, 318 m (1,043 ft) across and 124 m (407 ft) deep. It has a surface area of 70,650 square metres (760,500 sq ft).

landmarks.name: Leptis Magna
landmarks.description: Ancient city in modern Libya
landmarks.summary: Leptis or Lepcis Magna, also known by other names in antiquity, was a prominent city of the Carthaginian Empire and Roman Libya at the mouth of the Wadi Lebda in the Mediterranean.

landmarks.name: Ngorongoro Crater
landmarks.description: Protected area and a World Heritage Site in Arusha Region, Tanzania
landmarks.summary: Ngorongoro Conservation Area is a protected area and a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Ngorongoro District, 180 km (110 mi) west of Arusha City in Arusha Region, within the Crater Highlands geological area of northeastern Tanzania. The area is named after Ngorongoro Crater, a large volcanic caldera within the area.

landmarks.name: Lençóis Maranhenses
landmarks.description: National park in Maranhão, Brazil
landmarks.summary: Lençóis Maranhenses National Park is a national park in Maranhão state in northeastern Brazil, just east of the Baía de São José. Protected on June 2, 1981, the 155,000 ha (380,000-acre) park includes 70 km (43 mi) of coastline, and an interior composed of rolling sand dunes.

landmarks.name: Maasai Mara
landmarks.description: National Reserve in Narok County, Kenya
landmarks.summary: Maasai Mara, sometimes also spelt Masai Mara and locally known simply as the Mara, is a large national game reserve in Narok County, Kenya, contiguous with the Serengeti National Park in Tanzania. It is named in honour of the Maasai people, the ancestral inhabitants of the area, who migrated to the area from the Nile Basin.

credit.title: File:Sunset and clouds over Maasai Mara savanna landscape, Kenya.jpg
credit.author: Daniel Case

landmarks.name: Bagan
landmarks.description: UNESCO historical city in Mandalay Region, Myanmar
landmarks.summary: Bagan is a medieval city and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Mandalay Region of Myanmar. From the 9th to 13th centuries, the city was the capital of the Pagan Kingdom, the first kingdom that unified the regions that would later constitute Myanmar.

credit.title: File:Bagan, Burma.jpg
credit.author: Corto Maltese 1999
credit.credit: Originally uploaded to Flickr as View over the plain of Bagan

landmarks.name: Batu Caves
landmarks.description: Cave system in Gombak, Selangor, Malaysia
landmarks.summary: Batu Caves are a series of limestone caves in Gombak, Selangor, Malaysia. 1 mi) north of the Malaysian capital of Kuala Lumpur. The cave complex contains many Hindu temples, the most popular of which is a shrine dedicated to Murugan, and is the focal point of the Tamil Hindu festival of Thaipusam in Malaysia.

landmarks.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
landmarks.description: Shinto shrine near Kyoto, Japan
landmarks.summary: Fushimi Inari-taisha is the head shrine of the kami Inari, located in Fushimi-ku, Kyoto, Japan. 5 mi) and take approximately 2 hours to walk up. It is unclear whether the mountain's name, Inariyama, or the shrine's name came first.

credit.author: Basile Morin

landmarks.name: Palenque
landmarks.description: Ancient Maya city-state in Chiapas, Mexico
landmarks.summary: Palenque, also anciently known in the Itzaʼ language as Lakamha, was a Maya city-state in southern Mexico that perished in the 8th century. The Palenque ruins date from ca. 226 BC to ca. 799 AD. After its decline, it was overgrown by the jungle of cedar, mahogany, and sapodilla trees, but has since been excavated and restored.

landmarks.name: Gateway of India
landmarks.description: Landmark monument in Mumbai, India
landmarks.summary: The Gateway of India is an arch-monument, completed in 1924, on the waterfront of Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. It was erected to commemorate the landing of King George V of the United Kingdom for his coronation as the Emperor of India in December 1911 at Strand Road near Wellington Fountain. He was the first British monarch to visit India.

landmarks.name: Copacabana Beach
landmarks.description: Neighborhood of Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
landmarks.summary: Copacabana is a Brazilian bairro (neighbourhood) located in the South Zone of the city of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. 5 mile) balneario beach, which is one of the most famous in the world.

credit.author: [www.flickr.com/photos/26912057@N02/ bisonlux]

landmarks.name: Shibam
landmarks.description: Town in Hadhramaut, Yemen
landmarks.summary: Shibam, officially the Old Walled City of Shibam, is a town in Wadi Hadhramaut in eastern Yemen with about 7,000 inhabitants. It is the seat of the Shibam District in the Hadhramaut Governorate. It is known for its mudbrick-made high-rise buildings, with some of the buildings reaching as high as eleven stories.

landmarks.name: Amber Fort
landmarks.description: World Heritage Site in India
landmarks.summary: Amer Fort or Amber Fort is a fort located in Amer, Rajasthan, India. 8 mi) from Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan. Located high on a hill, it is the principal tourist attraction in Jaipur. Amer Fort is known for its artistic style elements.

landmarks.name: Lake Bled
landmarks.description: Lake in northwestern Slovenia
landmarks.summary: Lake Bled is a lake in the Julian Alps of the Upper Carniolan region of northwestern Slovenia, where it adjoins the town of Bled. The area is a tourist destination. The lake is 35 km (22 mi) from Ljubljana International Airport and 55 km (34 mi) from the capital city, Ljubljana. 6 mi) from the Lesce–Bled train station.

landmarks.name: Chefchaouen
landmarks.description: City in Tangier-Tetouan-Al Hoceima, Morocco
landmarks.summary: Chefchaouen is a city in northwest Morocco. It is the chief town of the province of the same name and is noted for its buildings in shades of blue, for which it is nicknamed the "Blue City". It is situated in a mountainous region in northern Morocco, between Tétouan and Ouazzane.

landmarks.name: Stari Most
landmarks.description: Bridge in Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina
landmarks.summary: The Old Bridge, also known as the Mostar Bridge, is a rebuilt 16th-century Ottoman bridge in the city of Mostar in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It crosses the river Neretva and connects the two parts of the city, which is named after the bridge keepers who guarded the Old Bridge during the Ottoman era.

landmarks.name: Wadi Rum
landmarks.description: Valley in southern Jordan
landmarks.summary: Wadi Rum (Arabic: وادي رم Wādī Ramm, also Wādī al-Ramm, known also as the Valley of the Moon or Red mountains, is a valley cut into the sandstone and granite rock in southern Jordan, near the border with Saudi Arabia and about 60 km to the east of the city of Aqaba. With an area of 720 km2 it is the largest wadi in Jordan.

landmarks.name: Hassan II Mosque
landmarks.description: Mosque in Casablanca, Morocco
landmarks.summary: The Hassan II Mosque is a mosque in Casablanca, Morocco. It is the second largest mosque in Africa and one of the largest mosques in the world. Its minaret is the world's second tallest minaret at 210 metres (689 ft).

credit.author: Milamber's portfolio
credit.credit: Sunshine on mosque Hassan II in Casablanca, Morocco

landmarks.name: Huangshan (Yellow Mountain)
landmarks.description: Mountain range in southern Anhui, China
landmarks.summary: Huangshan, literally meaning the Yellow Mountain(s), is a mountain range in southern Anhui province in eastern China. It was originally called "Yishan", and it was renamed because of a legend that the Yellow Emperor once made alchemy here.

landmarks.name: Tōdai-ji
landmarks.description: Buddhist temple in Nara, Japan
landmarks.summary: Tōdai-ji is a Buddhist temple complex that was once one of the powerful Seven Great Temples, located in the city of Nara, Japan. The construction of the temple was an attempt to imitate Chinese temples from the much-admired Tang dynasty. Though it was originally founded in the year 738 CE, Tōdai-ji was not opened until the year 752 CE.

landmarks.name: Sugarloaf Mountain
landmarks.description: Peak in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
landmarks.summary: Sugarloaf Mountain is a peak situated in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on a peninsula at the mouth of Guanabara Bay. Rising 396 m (1,299 ft) above the harbor, the peak is named for its resemblance to the traditional shape of concentrated refined sugarloaf. It is known worldwide for its cable car and panoramic views of the city and beyond.

credit.author: Arne Müseler

landmarks.name: Oriental Pearl Tower
landmarks.description: TV tower in Shanghai, China
landmarks.summary: The Oriental Pearl Tower is a futurist TV tower in Lujiazui, Shanghai. Built from 1991 to 1994, the tower was the tallest structure in China until the completion of nearby World Financial Center in 2007.
